mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it may indicate a restrictive monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and investment, thus causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows when FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong economic demand, which may boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following increases in both GDPC1 and HOUST, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion may indicate supply chain resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following an INDPRO increase during a late-cycle expansion, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following an RSAFS increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) may indicate a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a PAYEMS increase > 100,000, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it may indicate a tightening labor market and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows when FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE decreases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an early-cycle recovery may indicate improving consumer confidence and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a HOUST increase during an early-cycle recovery, this hypothesis is rejected.
